title: Real-time, cell-resolution guidance that makes incomplete cancer surgery uncommon

concept.text: The proposed innovation is a surgical guidance system that identifies residual malignant cells at the cut edges of a tumor while the operation is still underway. It would provide cellular detail across the operative margins, distinguish cancer from surrounding normal tissue, and locate remaining disease precisely enough for the surgeon to consider further excision during the same operation. The intended scope is the common operable solid cancers.

The defining advance would combine comprehensive coverage, cellular resolution, reliable tumor-to-normal discrimination and timely, actionable guidance. Finding an additional fluorescent lesion, classifying a selected tissue sample or imaging an excised specimen can contribute to this goal, but each establishes a narrower capability than detecting residual malignant cells throughout a surgical wound. The 2024 review distinguishes useful in situ fluorescence guidance from specimen imaging, which can provide better diagnostic performance under more controlled conditions.

significance.text: Residual malignant tissue at a surgical margin is an important contributor to local recurrence, although clear margins alone do not determine cure. A 2024 review reports initial positive margins in approximately 20% of head and neck cancer operations and involved margins in approximately 10% of breast-conservation operations. These are review-reported estimates for particular clinical settings, rather than universal rates. Existing surgical assessment already combines physical, radiological and pathological information, including intraoperative frozen sections and postoperative examination of the specimen.

If comprehensive detection enabled safe removal of residual disease, it could substantially reduce avoidable incomplete resections, repeat operations and local recurrences attributable to cells left at the cut edge. Partial fluorescence guidance already provides a concrete example of this potential: the supplied 2023 breast-lumpectomy trial abstract reports that second surgeries were avoided in 9 of 62 patients with positive margins. That result supports the clinical rationale without establishing the broader innovation's effectiveness across cancers.

Conditional impact assessment: making incomplete resection uncommon would change the reliability of surgery as a local cancer treatment. More precise guidance might also preserve healthy tissue and function, but that benefit requires clinical verification. Detection cannot guarantee safe removal when disease abuts critical structures or when additional excision would cause unacceptable harm. Consequently, even excellent imaging would not by itself establish an uncommon incomplete-resection rate.

Scope limit: this capability would address disease within the operative field. It would not eliminate malignant cells that have already disseminated, eradicate dormant cells elsewhere in the body or guarantee cure. No numerical reduction in overall cancer mortality can be inferred from the supplied margin-detection evidence.

missing_breakthrough.text: The target capability is comprehensive, real-time detection of residual malignant cells across operative margins with sufficient specificity and spatial precision to guide safe further excision. The supplied evidence documents useful but incomplete approaches at the sources' dates; it does not establish the availability or absence of this broader capability as of November 1, 2026.

Documented optical barriers include limited tissue penetration, background autofluorescence, selective accumulation of fluorescent probes in tumors, and reliable detection and interpretation of signals. A clinically useful signal must distinguish malignant tissue from normal tissue while remaining informative in the operative environment. Cellular detail in a selected field does not establish that the system has adequately examined the full margin, including disease beyond the accessible optical depth.

Available approaches are more varied than receptor- or enzyme-specific dyes. The supplied review describes receptor-targeted, intracellular-targeted, metabolic, microenvironment-sensitive and label-free approaches. Its supplement discusses ONM-100, or pegsitacianine, which exploits tumor-associated acidity across diverse tumor types. Such approaches may broaden applicability, but the supplied material does not demonstrate comprehensive single-cell margin detection. False-positive signal is a concern for actionable guidance; the narrower claim that inflammation specifically causes it is not established by the supplied reviewed texts.

Engineering synthesis: the remaining challenge includes turning detection into dependable surgical decisions. A system would need to connect its cellular findings to exact locations in the wound, maintain adequate coverage within an acceptable operating time, communicate uncertainty and avoid prompting harmful excision of healthy tissue. Its practical boundaries would need to identify margins that cannot be adequately assessed and disease that can be detected but cannot safely be removed.

current_state.text: The supplied 2023 prospective breast-lumpectomy trial demonstrates a meaningful partial capability. Pegulicianine-guided excisions removed residual tumor after standard lumpectomy in 27 of 357 patients, or 7.6%. Per-margin sensitivity was 49.3% and specificity was 85.2%. The trial met its prespecified thresholds for residual-tumor removal and specificity, but did not meet its prespecified sensitivity threshold. These measurements concern margins and patients in this application; they do not establish detection of every malignant cell.

The trial evidence available to the supplied review was a PubMed abstract rather than the full trial report. The abstract also states that randomization was not designed to provide a control group for evaluating device performance. The results therefore support additional residual-tumor detection and the reported performance measures, while leaving broader comparative outcome claims beyond what this supplied record establishes.

The 2024 review documents clinically used fluorescent agents, including 5-aminolevulinic acid, and a wider range of targeted and microenvironment-sensitive probes. It describes in situ fluorescence imaging as useful for surgical guidance and finding subclinical lesions, while ex vivo specimen imaging can achieve better diagnostic efficacy. Together with the breast trial, this supports the demonstrated component: selected applications can reveal disease missed by standard assessment. It does not establish comprehensive cellular certainty across operative margins and cancer types.

Several additional assertions in the earlier research remain unverified within the supplied evidence: FDA approval of pafolacianine for specified ovarian and lung indications, the glioma-specific history of 5-aminolevulinic acid, a 32.7% false-positive rate in an ovarian pafolacianine phase 3 experience, and confocal optical-biopsy accuracy often exceeding 80% in selected tissues. The cited Journal of Nuclear Medicine and ScienceDirect texts were not captured, so these statements are retained as unresolved reports rather than established findings. The Journal of Nuclear Medicine citation is identified in the research as 2026 and cannot substantiate attribution to a 2024 review. Missing evidence here does not show that the reported results are false.

The supplied review reports successful retention of the 2024 Nature article's full HTML, main PDF and a text-bearing supplement, superseding the earlier research note about failed full-page retrieval. Minor extraction artifacts remained, and figures were not visually inspected. Two additional supplementary PDFs contained essentially no extractable text and provide no inspectable support here. No freshness search was supplied, so the dated findings cannot establish the complete state of the field on November 1, 2026.

completion_criteria.text: Proposed initial clinical demonstration: prospective controlled surgical trials in at least two different operable solid tumors should show clinically meaningful reductions in incomplete resection and subsequent local recurrence attributable to residual disease at the margin, compared with standard care that includes usual visualization and pathology. Trials should prespecify effect sizes, recurrence follow-up, healthy-tissue removal and harms from false-positive excisions. These are proposed criteria for this innovation, not established regulatory or professional standards.
completion_criteria.label: Reduced incomplete resection and local recurrence across two solid tumors

completion_criteria.text: Proposed technical validation: independently verify cellular resolution, tumor-to-normal discrimination, depth limits, coverage of the operative margins and response time under actual surgical conditions, using pathological comparison where feasible. Evaluation should distinguish per-cell, per-region, per-margin and per-patient performance so that a strong result at one scale is not mistaken for comprehensive performance at another. Sensitivity around one half of involved margins in one cancer would not satisfy the proposed comprehensive capability.
completion_criteria.label: Independent verification of comprehensive cellular-resolution margin assessment during surgery

completion_criteria.text: Proposed reproducibility and breadth requirements: independent teams and multiple clinical sites should reproduce the technical and clinical benefits across relevant tissue conditions, tumor subtypes and surgical workflows. Success in two cancers would establish initial breadth; broader validation would be needed to support applicability across common operable cancers. Finite testing can establish the breadth demonstrated, never literal detection of every malignant cell in every possible case.
completion_criteria.label: Independent multisite reproduction of technical and clinical benefits across cancers

completion_criteria.text: Proposed practical endpoint: demonstrate that incomplete resection becomes uncommon within clearly specified clinical populations, while preserving acceptable function, healthy tissue and operative time. Report residual failures separately, including missed disease, inadequately assessed margins and detected disease that cannot safely be excised. A reduction in positive margins alone would not establish lower recurrence or the title's intended outcome.
completion_criteria.label: Incomplete resection becomes uncommon in clearly specified clinical populations

related_concepts.text: Roster-based synthesis: ONC-01, mortality-reducing detection of lethal cancers while localized, concerns finding disease early enough for effective treatment; ONC-11 concerns the completeness of surgical removal once an operation is undertaken. ONC-10, distinguishing early neoplasms that will kill from those that will not, addresses whether treatment is warranted. More sensitive margin guidance does not establish a tumor's lethality or resolve overtreatment.

Roster-based synthesis: ONC-02 concerns sterilizing immune clearance of established metastatic carcinomas, while ONC-03 concerns eradication of dormant disseminated tumor cells responsible for late relapse. ONC-11 addresses local operative margins and could complement either systemic advance. It does not clear established metastases or dormant cells outside the operative field. The supplied roster provides these distinctions more precisely than the earlier shorthand linking ONC-02 to micrometastases alone.

Roster-based synthesis: ONC-04 seeks a shared malignant dependency that renewing normal tissues can spare, and ONC-05 seeks therapies that extinguish the whole clonal population. Both overlap with ONC-11's need to distinguish malignant from normal tissue and avoid leaving viable cancer behind, but their central goals concern therapeutic selectivity and population extinction. ONC-06 instead seeks stable reversion of carcinoma cells to non-malignant identity; surgical guidance identifies tissue for possible removal rather than changing its identity.

Roster-based synthesis: ONC-07 seeks body-wide delivery that alters essentially every malignant cell. Probe delivery may enable some forms of ONC-11, but signal generation within a surgical field does not demonstrate body-wide therapeutic delivery. ONC-12 seeks off-the-shelf cell therapy that matches autologous cures at ordinary scale; it is a distinct treatment and manufacturing challenge that could complement local surgery.

Roster-based synthesis: ONC-08 concerns interception of non-viral precancers before invasion, and ONC-09 concerns prophylactic immunity against common non-viral cancers. Both act earlier in disease development than ONC-11's operative-margin intervention. Their success might reduce the need for some cancer operations, while margin guidance would remain relevant to cancers requiring resection.

unresolved_issues: The complete state of the field as of November 1, 2026 remains unassessed because no freshness search was supplied.

The uncaptured Journal of Nuclear Medicine and ScienceDirect sources leave the stated FDA indications, glioma-specific agent history, ovarian 32.7% false-positive rate and confocal accuracy above 80% unverified within this record.
The denominator and analytical definition underlying the reported ovarian 32.7% false-positive rate cannot be determined from the supplied material.
Full trial methods, longer-term recurrence outcomes and broader comparative conclusions cannot be assessed from the supplied pegulicianine abstract alone.

The degree to which comprehensive detection could make incomplete resection uncommon, preserve healthy tissue or improve survival remains to be demonstrated, particularly where safe excision is anatomically constrained.
Specific numerical targets for acceptable residual failure, tissue removal, operative time and false-positive harms remain to be proposed and justified for each clinical setting.

The review's option to remove unverified ancillary claims was not followed literally: their numerical details were retained as explicitly unresolved reports to preserve the supplied research's quantitative information without endorsing it.

brief.title: Finding cancer cells left behind during surgery
possible: During cancer surgery, surgeons could see malignant cells left along the cut edges while there is still time to remove them. Guidance would cover the whole surgical wound, distinguish cancer from healthy tissue and pinpoint remaining disease closely enough to guide further removal.
why: For people having surgery for common solid cancers, this could mean fewer repeat operations and fewer cancers returning near the original site because cells were left behind.
More precise guidance could also help surgeons preserve healthy tissue and the functions it supports.

sources.who: Han Cheng, Hongtao Xu and colleagues
sources.showed: Their review describes fluorescence imaging, which uses light emitted by tissue or added agents to reveal cancer during surgery. It identifies limits in tissue penetration, cancer selectivity and signal interpretation.
sources.cited_for: Light-based guidance can reveal otherwise hidden disease, but comprehensive assessment during surgery faces unresolved technical barriers.
sources.not_established: The review does not demonstrate reliable detection of individual cancer cells throughout a surgical wound.

sources.showed: Their breast surgery trial used pegulicianine, a fluorescent drug, to guide extra tissue removal. This approach, called pFGS, found cancer left after standard surgery but missed about half of affected cut edges.
sources.quote: The use of pFGS in breast cancer surgery met prespecified thresholds for removal of residual tumor
sources.cited_for: Fluorescence guidance can help surgeons remove cancer missed during standard breast surgery.
sources.not_established: The trial does not establish comprehensive cell detection or controlled evidence of fewer local recurrences across cancers.

shown: Barbara L Smith and colleagues showed that fluorescence guidance helped remove cancer left after standard breast surgery in 7.6% of patients receiving it. Some patients avoided another operation, but the approach missed about half of affected cut edges.
missing: A system has yet to demonstrate reliable detection of individual cancer cells across the whole wound, including its assessable depth.
Findings must map precisely to locations surgeons can act on, within an acceptable operating time and without harmful removal of healthy tissue.
Controlled trials must establish fewer incomplete removals and local recurrences, with benefits reproduced independently across common operable cancers.

milestones.label: Less incomplete removal and local recurrence across two cancers
milestones.explanation: Controlled trials would have to show fewer incomplete removals and local recurrences across two solid cancers, while tracking harms. This would establish an initial clinical benefit over standard care.

milestones.label: Independent confirmation of whole-wound guidance at individual-cell detail
milestones.explanation: Independent testing during surgery would have to confirm individual-cell detail, cancer recognition, coverage, depth limits and response time. This would establish whether guidance reliably assesses the whole wound.

milestones.label: Independent teams reproduce benefits across cancers and hospitals
milestones.explanation: Independent teams at multiple hospitals would have to reproduce technical and clinical benefits across cancers and surgical conditions. This would establish how broadly the system works.

milestones.label: Incomplete cancer removal becomes uncommon in defined patient groups
milestones.explanation: Studies would have to show uncommon incomplete removal with acceptable function, tissue loss and operating time, while explaining remaining failures. This would establish the intended practical outcome.

uncertain: How often would detecting remaining cancer allow safe removal when it lies beside structures that cannot be damaged?
What failure rate, tissue loss, operating time and harm from false alarms would be acceptable for each cancer?
Would comprehensive guidance preserve healthy tissue and improve survival?

page.title: Intraoperative microscopic imaging of residual cancer
page.definition: After the surgeon removes a tumour, a microscope images tissue in the resection cavity, the wound left inside the patient. Software classifies the images and shows the surgeon where residual cancer can be excised before closure. The microscope may examine the whole cavity or regions selected by an objective signal. Final pathology assesses the cut edges of the removed tissue using the margin criteria for that cancer.

goal.need: In US registry data from 2004 to 2020, 16.1% of 60,695 patients with oral cavity cancer and 33.1% of 31,950 with oropharyngeal cancer had positive margins. After breast lumpectomy, pathology can reveal an involved margin days later, when further excision requires another operation. Even a rapid reading of the specimen leaves the surgeon to find the matching spot in the wound. Locating residual cancer there before closure could spare a patient another operation when the surgeon can safely remove more tissue.

completion.title: Microscopic cavity guidance reduces final positive surgical margins to no more than 2%.
completion.criterion: An automated system locates residual cancer by microscopy in the resection cavity, guides further excision during the operation and reduces the final positive-margin rate to ≤2%. PSI requires demonstration of the in vivo workflow in two cancer types. It sets no clinical sample size or confidence-bound rule for the 2% target.
completion.set_by: ARPA-H, PSI solicitation 75N99223R0004, section 1.2.1, Cancer localization; amended 17 November 2023.
completion.threshold_quote: will reduce positive margins during oncological surgery to no more than 2%.
completion.basis: ARPA-H sets the 2% surgical outcome for its cancer-localization programme. Technical Area 1-B specifies animal validation of the in vivo workflow and permits objective selection of regions for microscopy. Diagnostic accuracy in those regions and final margin status after surgery are distinct outcomes.

milestones.title: A laboratory cavity-imaging prototype prepares and images a region within 30 minutes.
milestones.criterion: A breadboard prototype completes site preparation and imaging in 30 minutes per region of interest.
milestones.set_by: ARPA-H PSI, TA1-B Phase 1 proof-of-concept requirements.

milestones.title: Automated cavity imaging achieves ≥98% sensitivity and ≥95% specificity in animal models.
milestones.criterion: Demonstrate these diagnostic targets in rodent and large-animal disease models covering two cancer types, against a pathologist’s formalin-fixed, paraffin-embedded histology assessment. PSI specifies ≤0.5 µm imaging resolution and final evaluation times below 3 minutes per region or 10 minutes per entire field.
milestones.set_by: ARPA-H PSI, TA1-B minimum specifications and Phase 2 validation requirements.

milestones.title: An initial human study establishes safety and distinguishes tumour from normal tissue in the cavity.
milestones.criterion: In patients undergoing tumour resection, assess the safety of the imaging procedure and its ability to distinguish residual tumour from normal tissue at imaged sites in the cavity. Compare the image findings with histology from corresponding sites. The society specifies no universal numerical accuracy threshold.
milestones.set_by: International Society of Image Guided Surgery, consensus report, Early-Phase Clinical Endpoints and Conclusion; written for fluorescence navigation.
milestones.threshold_quote: clearly delineate normal from tumor tissues

milestones.title: Image-guided additional excision lowers the proportion of patients with involved surgical margins.
milestones.criterion: Show that additional excision guided by cavity imaging reduces the proportion of patients with at least one positive margin on final histology. State the comparator and apply the same cancer-specific definition of a positive margin to both assessments. The society lists change in positive-margin rate as a possible secondary endpoint and sets no minimum effect size.
milestones.set_by: International Society of Image Guided Surgery, Advanced-Phase Clinical Endpoints; improvement is the direction specified by ARPA-H PSI.
milestones.threshold_quote: change in rate of positive margins

milestones.title: A regulator authorizes cavity guidance for intraoperative residual-cancer detection in a specified operation.
milestones.criterion: Obtain marketing authorization whose indication includes adjunctive detection of residual cancer in the patient's resection cavity during the specified operation after removal of the primary specimen. Apply the authorization only to its labelled population, procedure and device–agent combination where applicable.
milestones.set_by: US FDA, premarket approval P230014; the cited authorization applies specifically to breast lumpectomy.
milestones.threshold_quote: intraoperative detection of cancerous tissue within the resection cavity following removal of the primary

milestones.title: An integrated cavity microscope images a region of interest within 10 minutes.
milestones.criterion: By programme month 48, complete the integrated device and image a region of interest in the resection cavity within 10 minutes. This timing covers image acquisition.
milestones.set_by: ARPA-H Precision Surgical Interventions, Technical Area 1-B, Phase 2 integrated-device target

milestones.title: Automated cavity microscopy reaches ≥98% sensitivity and ≥95% specificity in animal models.
milestones.criterion: By programme month 54, classify cavity images with ≥98% sensitivity and ≥95% specificity against one pathologist’s reading of formalin-fixed, paraffin-embedded tissue. Test the workflow in at least two cancer types using a rodent and a large-animal disease model. PSI permits alternative metrics for a particular case if supported by a power analysis and a quantified improvement over current practice.
milestones.set_by: ARPA-H Precision Surgical Interventions, Technical Area 1-B, Phase 2 classifier validation

milestones.title: Cavity evaluation takes under 3 minutes per region or under 10 minutes for the whole field.
milestones.criterion: By programme month 60, complete imaging and automated classification at resolution ≤0.5 µm in under 3 minutes per objectively selected region or under 10 minutes for the whole field. PSI specifies a 2 cm × 2 cm reference region or equivalent circular area and scales imaging time down in proportion to area for smaller regions. Cavity preparation may take up to 5 additional minutes.
milestones.set_by: ARPA-H Precision Surgical Interventions, Technical Area 1-B, minimum specifications and Phase 2 final timing target
milestones.threshold_quote: in less than 10/3 minutes (+5 min sample prep)

not_found: No published demonstration was identified combining automated cavity microscopy, the PSI diagnostic targets and ≤2% final positive margins in two cancer types.
No external completion criterion was found requiring single-cell detection throughout the entire surgical wound or specifying a universal assessment depth.
The original PSI attachment did not render on SAM.gov; the cited solicitation text is its GovTribe transcription.
The supplied Journal of Nuclear Medicine PDF and ScienceDirect page returned access errors.

results.finding: Blinded readers assessing 50 excised-tissue images achieved 91.7% sensitivity.
results.detail: Specificity was 92.1%. Images were classified by human readers, not automatically; the assessment used excised human tissue rather than cavity imaging in rodent and large-animal models. Resolution was approximately 9 µm.
results.quote: Overall, the analysis resulted in sensitivity of 91.7% (95% CI: 62.5–100%) and specificity of 92.1% (95% CI: 78.4–98%).

results.finding: In 60 oral-cancer patients, reflectance confocal microscopy had 90.2% sensitivity for tumor identification.
results.detail: An expert manually classified images from tumor and surrounding mucosa before resection. The study did not test automated cavity imaging in rodent and large-animal models; sensitivity was below the 98% target.
results.quote: The sensitivity for identifying tumors was 90.2% (95% CI, 78.6%–96.7%), and the positive predictive value was also 90.2% (95% CI, 78.6%–96.7%).

results.finding: Manual assessment of 169 images from 5 patients achieved 89.9% sensitivity.
results.detail: Specificity was 78.6%. Images were classified by clinicians, not an automated system; this was a human study of one cancer type, and the probe resolution was 1 µm.
results.quote: In summary, we could show an accuracy, sensitivity, specificity, PPV and NPV of 85.8%, 89.9%, 78.6%, 87.9% and 81.9%, respectively.

results.finding: In 357 patients undergoing fluorescence-guided breast lumpectomy, per-margin sensitivity was 49.3%.
results.detail: Surgeons excised additional cavity margins at sites with a pegulicianine signal.
results.quote: On per-margin analysis, pFGS specificity was 85.2%, and sensitivity was 49.3%.

results.finding: Fluorescence-guided excision avoided second surgery in 9 of 62 breast lumpectomy patients with positive margins.
results.detail: The trial used 10:1 randomization to discourage smaller initial excisions in anticipation of imaging. The authors state that randomization was not designed to provide a control group for evaluating device performance.
results.quote: Second surgeries were avoided by pFGS in 9 of 62 patients with positive margins.

results.finding: The laboratory prototype acquired three ex vivo human breast confocal mosaics in about 7 seconds each. The number of donors was unstated.
results.detail: The 30-second staining step excludes rinsing and probe positioning. The paper reports it separately from the timed mosaic examples.
results.quote:
Acquisition times were approximately 7 s for (a,b,e),

results.finding: Integrated handheld OCT acquired breast resection-bed video at 11.5 frames/s in a 35-patient study.
results.detail: The surgeon manually swept the probe across the cavity. The paper gives no elapsed time for a complete regional sweep.
results.quote: the handheld OCT probe system presented here provides a transverse scan range of 8.8 mm and an imaging rate of 11.5 frames per second.

results.finding: Handheld breast cavity OCT had approximately 9 µm axial and transverse resolution in a 35-patient study.
results.quote: the 2D OCT images (B-scans) are displayed on the computer screen with axial and transverse resolutions of approximately 9 μm, an image width of 8.8 mm, and a frame rate of 11.5 frames/s.

results.finding: Handheld breast cavity OCT distinguished tumour from normal tissue in two representative patients with supporting histology.
results.detail: The reported sensitivity and specificity came from excised specimens. The in vivo findings were qualitative.
results.quote: Final post-operative histological analysis, however, confirmed the intraoperative OCT finding of a negative margin, which meant that the additional normal tissue was removed unnecessarily.

results.finding: Handheld confocal imaging of two pre-resection oral sites averaged 10 minutes in 44 timed patients.
results.detail: The mean across two sites does not establish a per-region acquisition time.
results.quote: The average time spent on imaging was 10 ± 4 minutes, which was considered not to be disruptive to the normal workflow of the operating room.

results.finding: In 60 oral cancer patients, blinded confocal readings achieved 90.2% sensitivity at pre-resection tumour-targeted sites.
results.detail: The sensitivity comes from the main Results section and applies to tumour-targeted sites. The surgeon did not use the images to change the resection.
results.quote: The sensitivity for identifying tumors was 90.2% (95% CI, 78.6%–96.7%), and the positive predictive value was also 90.2% (95% CI, 78.6%–96.7%).

results.finding: Intraoperative confocal laser endomicroscopy in 5 patients with oropharyngeal cancer averaged 5 min 20 s of image acquisition per case.
results.detail: The discussion also describes post-resection imaging of histologically benign pharyngeal sites, with no separate timing for those sites.
results.quote: The average image acquisition time for each case was 5 min, 20 s (range: 4 min 5 s–7 min 17 s).

results.finding: In 5 patients with oropharyngeal cancer, blinded readers achieved 85.8% accuracy on 169 selected confocal images with corresponding histology.
results.detail: The main examination preceded tumour removal. Readers classified selected high-quality images postoperatively.
results.quote: In summary, we could show an accuracy, sensitivity, specificity, PPV and NPV of 85.8%, 89.9%, 78.6%, 87.9% and 81.9%, respectively.

results.finding: Claire-aided assessment in 206 lumpectomy patients had 24.62% sensitivity at excised margins.
results.detail: The margin-level accuracy estimates describe surgeon decisions aided by Claire after standard-of-care assessment. The device had no direct patient contact.
results.quote:
for the 1,335 device-assessable margins from the full analysis set, showed a 
sensitivity of 24.62% and a specificity of 91.34%, with a negative predictive value (NPV) of 95.95% and 
a lower positive predictive value (PPV) at 13.22% (Table 7).

results.finding: Claire-guided shaves reduced the positive-margin rate by 3.4 percentage points in 206 lumpectomy patients.
results.detail: This was a within-patient comparison in the device arm. Positive margins were defined using NCCN and SSO/ASTRO guidelines.
results.quote:
In the full analysis set (FAS) (N=206), at least one unaddressed positive margin was identified in 35 
participants following SOC procedures and in 28 participants after the completion of SOC and 
device procedures (Figure 4, Table 4).

results.finding: FDA approved Claire OCT for adjunctive ex vivo lumpectomy margin assessment on March 3, 2026.
results.quote: CDRH issued an approval order on March 3, 2026.

results.finding: Among 54 patients undergoing L-ICG fluorescence-guided breast-conserving surgery, 0 serious adverse events were observed.
results.quote: No serious adverse events were observed.

results.finding: Among 54 patients undergoing L-ICG fluorescence-guided breast-conserving surgery, 1.9% had positive margins on final histopathology.
results.quote: This further reduced the positive margin rate to 1.9% at final histopathology.

results.finding: FDA approved Lumicell DVS with LUMISIGHT for residual cancer detection in the breast lumpectomy cavity on April 17, 2024. The letter gives no clinical sample size.
results.quote:
fluorescence imaging of the lumpectomy cavity. Based upon the information submitted, the PMA is 
approved.

results.finding: Handheld QME in 21 breast surgery patients acquired each 3D cavity scan in 3.3 seconds.
results.detail: The reported time covers acquisition of one 3D volume.
results.quote: The acquisition time for each 3D scan was 3.3 seconds.

results.finding: Breast cavity QME in 21 patients acquired a local 3D scan in 3.3 seconds.
results.detail: Real-time stiffness mapping provides an input to cancer classification. The study gives no timing for the subsequent cancer evaluation.
results.quote: The acquisition time for each 3D scan was 3.3 seconds.

results.finding: In 21 breast surgery patients, cavity QME showed elevated stiffness in all 4 cancer-associated aspects.
results.detail: Validation used 23 direct cavity shavings and 2 adjacent positive excision margins. The other 13 scanned aspects lacked conclusive histologic validation.
results.quote:
In four cavity aspects
presenting cancer and 21 cavity aspects presenting benign tissue,
QME detected elevated stiffness in all four cancer cases, in contrast
to low stiffness observed in 19 of the 21 benign cases.

results.finding: AI classified oral squamous cell carcinoma images with 96.58% accuracy. Training set: 4,090 images.
results.detail: The patient count and the number of images used to estimate accuracy are unstated.
results.quote: The AI model achieved an area under the precision-recall curve (AUC-PR) of 0.99 and an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC-ROC) of 0.99, with sensitivity 98.09%, specificity 95.00%, accuracy 96.58%, positive predictive value (PPV) 95.35%, and negative predictive value (NPV) 97.94%.

results.finding: AI classified oral squamous cell carcinoma images with 98.09% sensitivity. Training set: 4,090 images.
results.detail: The patient count and the number of images used to estimate sensitivity and specificity are unstated.
results.quote: The AI model achieved an area under the precision-recall curve (AUC-PR) of 0.99 and an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC-ROC) of 0.99, with sensitivity 98.09%, specificity 95.00%, accuracy 96.58%, positive predictive value (PPV) 95.35%, and negative predictive value (NPV) 97.94%.

results.finding: Handheld QME acquired each 3D breast cavity scan in 3.3 seconds in a study of 21 patients.
results.quote: The acquisition time for each 3D scan was 3.3 seconds.

results.finding: Handheld QME acquired each local breast cavity scan in 3.3 seconds in a study of 21 patients.
results.detail: Surgeons selected predominantly dense tissue during a brief survey. The reported time covers a single scan and excludes the survey and subsequent cancer evaluation.
results.quote: The acquisition time for each 3D scan was 3.3 seconds.

results.finding: In a 21-patient breast surgery study, in vivo QME showed elevated stiffness at all 4 histology-supported cancer sites.
results.detail: Two cancer sites were supported by histology from cavity shavings and two by histology from adjacent positive specimen margins. Histology was inconclusive for 13 of the 38 scanned cavity aspects.
results.quote: In four cavity aspects presenting cancer and 21 cavity aspects presenting benign tissue, QME detected elevated stiffness in all four cancer cases, in contrast to low stiffness observed in 19 of the 21 benign cases.

results.finding: A chip-scale prototype imaged residual breast tumor in one mouse tissue section with a 40 ms integration time.
results.detail: The reported time measures sensor integration. The paper describes fluorescent labeling and manual illumination setup separately, without reporting an end-to-end time per region.
results.quote: A focus of tumor with diameter close to 500 μm is detected with a very high 45 dB SNR and an integration time of only 40 ms.

results.finding: Confocal endomicroscopy during sinonasal melanoma resection in 2 patients captured approximately 5 minutes of video per patient.
results.detail: The study used a commercial Cellvizio system with a flexible miniprobe. Video duration measures footage captured across the case, while added operating time measures the broader examination.
results.quote: During the endoscopic resection, approximately 5 min of CLE video was captured for each patient, from which several hundred images were extracted.

results.finding: In 2 sinonasal melanoma patients, confocal laser endomicroscopy correctly classified 6 of 10 post-resection cavity-margin images as healthy.
results.detail: Blood and coagulation remnants complicated cavity-margin interpretation even after the authors selected high-quality images.
results.quote: Here, 6 out of 10 images were correctly identified as healthy mucosa, 3 were marked as uncertain, and 1 image was misclassified as containing tumor cells, despite histopathological evaluation showing no residual tumor cells.

results.finding: In an interim breast lumpectomy study with 18 analysed cases, Optiscan reported zero adverse events related to intravenous fluorescein.
results.detail: Safety reporting covers fluorescein injections. The margin counts describe the analysed cases and cannot establish cavity-site diagnostic performance.
results.quote:
There have been no reported 
adverse events related to intravenous sodium fluorescein contrast agent injections.

results.finding: Among 357 breast lumpectomy patients, LUMISIGHT-guided shaves converted 14.5% of those with positive standard-surgery margins to all-negative final margins.
results.detail: The 14.5% is the conversion rate among the 62 patients with positive margins after standard surgery. The 35 randomized controls were outside the efficacy analysis.
results.quote:
Converting 9 of 62 (14.5%) patients with SoC positive margins to final negative 
margins by excising LUM-guided shaves.

definition = "After the surgeon removes a tumour, a microscope images tissue in the resection cavity, the wound left inside the patient. Software classifies the images and shows the surgeon where residual cancer can be excised before closure. The microscope may examine the whole cavity or regions selected by an objective signal. Final pathology assesses the cut edges of the removed tissue using the margin criteria for that cancer.". Reason: The definition currently presents margin reduction as an established effect and leaves the distinction between the wound and the removed specimen implicit.

goal.need = "In US registry data from 2004 to 2020, 16.1% of 60,695 patients with oral cavity cancer and 33.1% of 31,950 with oropharyngeal cancer had positive margins. After breast lumpectomy, pathology can reveal an involved margin days later, when further excision requires another operation. Even a rapid reading of the specimen leaves the surgeon to find the matching spot in the wound. Locating residual cancer there before closure could spare a patient another operation when the surgeon can safely remove more tissue.". Reason: The current paragraph points to absent figures and omits the difficulty of finding the corresponding site in the wound.

add statement by Advanced Research Projects Agency for Health, Precision Surgical Interventions Proposers’ Day announcement, 2023: "intraoperative microscopic imaging of the resection cavity and automated image classification". Reason: The 2023 programme announcement names the specific technical goal that the broader 2024 statement describes.

edit completion: criterion = "An automated system locates residual cancer by microscopy in the resection cavity, guides further excision during the operation and reduces the final positive-margin rate to \u22642%. PSI requires demonstration of the in vivo workflow in two cancer types. It sets no clinical sample size or confidence-bound rule for the 2% target."; basis = "ARPA-H sets the 2% surgical outcome for its cancer-localization programme. Technical Area 1-B specifies animal validation of the in vivo workflow and permits objective selection of regions for microscopy. Diagnostic accuracy in those regions and final margin status after surgery are distinct outcomes."; refs = [4, 22]. Reason: The solicitation distinguishes the programme-wide surgical outcome from the two-cancer animal validation specified for its in vivo pathway.
add case "Prostate". Reason: PSI lists prostate cancer first in its preference order for in vivo validation and specifies integration with the surgical robot for that case.
add case "Ovarian". Reason: PSI explicitly names ovarian cancer as a first validation case for cavity imaging.

add milestone after m1: "An integrated cavity microscope images a region of interest within 10 minutes.". Reason: PSI sets an integrated-device imaging test between the laboratory prototype and validation of the classifier.
